name: Huexotzinco amate and maguey sheets
description: The 1531 Huexotzinco Codex includes writing and painting supports identified as both amate bark and maguey plant-fibre sheets.

impact.note: One codex whose sheets witness long-established Mesoamerican bark and maguey paper; the object itself changed nothing and had no successors.

date.label: 1531 codex
date.basis: Date of the stated witness or contextual sample, not a claim of global origin.

events.statement: The 1531 Huexotzinco Codex includes writing and painting supports identified as both amate bark and maguey plant-fibre sheets.

evidence.supports: Conservators identify four amate and four maguey supports in the 1531 codex and describe Mesoamerican beaten-fibre sheets using historical accounts. Their noninvasive examination does not identify specific sheet makers or prove how every sheet was prepared.

events.caveats: The document date witnesses use, while identification of plant substrates and manufacture derives from conservators’ technical examination and historical descriptions; it does not identify the maker, exact production date or an origin. Sheet beating differs from the suspended-fibre mould process in the existing papermaking record.
